title: role-taster-72hr-tryout-and-onboarding-protocol
content:
Purpose:

This doc describes a lightweight 72-hour role-taster (tryout) program for senior individual contributor and contractor candidates. The goal is to accelerate evidence collection about real on-the-job fit while giving candidates a tangible preview of the work, team, and cadence. This is intended to complement (not replace) behavioral interviews and a final hiring loop.

Scope and when to use:
- Target roles: mid-senior ICs, specialized contractors (design, product, infra, SRE, data infra). Not intended for junior/new-grad hires.
- Use cases: close-call candidates where we need more signal; expedited hiring for short-term projects; conversion trials for contracting-to-perm.
- Limit: 72-hour remote, paid short engagement (stipend). Not a full-time assignment.

Core principles:
1) Timebox: clear 72-hour scope and deliverables.
2) Transparency: candidate receives expectations, rubric, and pay info up front.
3) Low friction for the hiring team: pre-made task templates and an evaluator rota.
4) Candidate experience first: structured feedback and a debrief meeting regardless of outcome.

72-hour timeline (example):
Day 0 (pre-start): People Ops sends welcome packet, NDA (if required), stipend details, access checklist, and a single-sentence task brief.
Day 1: Kickoff (30–45m) with hiring manager + mentor. Candidate works on scoped task. Daily async check-in via Slack thread and short progress notes.
Day 2: Candidate continues work; scheduled 30-minute sync with mentor for clarifying Qs; evaluator reviews early artifacts.
Day 3: Finalize deliverable, record 15–20m walkthrough (optional), submit artifacts by 4pm. Final 60-minute debrief with hiring manager + two evaluators within 48 hours.

Compensation and logistics:
- Stipend: $350–$650 depending on seniority/role and expected time commitment (pro-rated).
- Legal: standard contractor template + brief IP clause for deliverables. People Ops owns contracting paperwork.
- Tools & access: temporary project repo, read-only production docs, staging dataset (anonymized). Access expires automatically after 7 days.

Deliverable templates (pick one per role):
- Design: 1–2 screens + rationale doc (max 2 pages) + clickable prototype links.
- Product/PM: 1–pager PRD + prioritization notes + 3 user flows.
- Infra/SRE: troubleshooting playbook for a simulated incident + short automation script.
- Data/ML infra: small ETL spec + sample ingestion pipeline (not full infra).
- Frontend/Backend: implement a focused API endpoint or UI component (~2–4 hours of dev time).

Evaluation rubric (5 dimensions, 1–5 scale):
1) Problem framing & correctness: did candidate understand scope and deliver workable solution?
2) Tradeoffs & reasoning: clarity of alternatives, constraints, and cost/benefit judgments.
3) Execution quality: code/artefact cleanliness, testability, UX clarity.
4) Collaboration & communication: clarity in updates, responsiveness to questions, openness to feedback.
5) Impact fit: evidence they would move a project forward within our org cadence.

Scoring and decision protocol:
- Each evaluator submits a numeric score (1–5) and a 3-sentence summary.
- Minimum 2 evaluators per trial (hiring manager + cross-functional reviewer).
- Decision matrix: average score >= 3.8 -> strong convert; 3.0–3.79 -> consider with discussion (hireable with reservations); <3.0 -> decline.
- Override path: hiring manager may escalate to director for narrow hires where team fit matters more than rubric score.

Evaluator checklist (pre-run):
- Confirm task template chosen and adjusted to 4–8 hours of focused work.
- Reserve 60 minutes for final debrief within 48 hours of submission.
- Prepare focused assessment questions (3 prompts per dimension).
- Ensure access to anonymized test data and project repo.

Hiring manager/mentor checklist (during run):
- Kickoff: clarify scope and success criteria in kickoff.
- Mid-run sync: 30m to unblock and observe approach. Avoid doing candidate work.
- Final debrief: ask candidate to present tradeoffs and next steps. Provide 10m for candidate Qs.

Candidate-facing template language (to send Day 0):
Title: 72-hour role taster — schedule and expectations
Hi [Candidate],
Thanks for agreeing to our 72-hour role taster. This is a paid, timeboxed exercise to help both of us evaluate fit. Below is what to expect: kickoff with [Manager] on [date], a focused task (estimated 4–8 hours total), one short mentor sync, and a final debrief. You will receive a stipend of [amount] after submission. If you have any access concerns, reply to this thread and we’ll resolve them within 24h.
Deliverables: [link to task brief]
Rubric: we evaluate problem framing, tradeoffs, execution, communication, and impact fit. We’ll share feedback within 48 hours of your final submission.
Best,
People Ops (Maya Chen)

Debrief template (manager->candidate):
- Start with strengths (2–3 bullets).
- Top 2 improvement areas with concrete examples.
- Clear next step recommendation (convert / contract extension / decline) and timing.
- Candidate questions & close.

Risk and fairness considerations:
- Accessibility: tasks must not require specific proprietary tools; provide alternatives for candidates who need assistive tech.
- Bias mitigation: anonymize nonessential identifiers in artifacts; rubrics standardized across evaluators.
- Comp time tracking: ensure no candidate is expected to exceed stated hours. Adjust stipend if requested.

Experiment metrics (for the pilot 3-month window):
- % of tryouts that convert to hires or contractor extensions.
- Time-to-offer for converted candidates vs control group.
- Candidate NPS (post-trial survey).
- Hiring manager satisfaction (post-debrief survey).
- Diversity signal: track demographic mix of participants to ensure no adverse selection.

Operational notes and next steps for People Ops:
- Pilot run: Q1 2026 with up to 12 trials across product, infra, and design.
- Build task-template library and stipend bands.
- Create short Confluence how-to and an intake form for hiring managers.
- Measure pilot metrics and iterate — decision whether to embed as standard flow after 3 months.

Appendix: sample short task brief (Design)
Context: We need a clearer onboarding microflow in the Redwood Console for first-time API users.
Deliverable: Propose a 1–2 screen flow (Figma links encouraged) and a 1-page rationale covering goals, success metrics, and two tradeoffs you considered.
Time estimate: 5–6 hours.
Evaluation focus: clarity of goals, measurable success metrics, QoL tradeoffs for engineering vs product, and polish of artifact.

-- End of document --
